beliefs.practice: Create one reusable PyMongo MongoClient per Flask worker process rather than creating a client for every request.
Initialize MongoClient after worker processes fork when deploying Flask under a prefork server such as Gunicorn.
Use the service-provided connection string, including its required hostname and connection options, rather than reconstructing it from assumptions about another MongoDB-compatible service.
Require TLS for database connections and leave certificate and hostname validation enabled; do not use tlsAllowInvalidCertificates or tlsAllowInvalidHostnames.
Set retryWrites=false in the Azure DocumentDB connection configuration rather than relying on PyMongo's default retryable-write behavior.
Configure finite serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, and socketTimeoutMS values consistent with the API's request deadline.
Set maxPoolSize and waitQueueTimeoutMS explicitly so concurrent Flask requests cannot create unbounded database connection pressure or wait indefinitely for a connection.
Configure appName on MongoClient so database diagnostics can identify connections from this application.
Percent-encode username and password components with urllib.parse.quote_plus when constructing a MongoDB connection URI.
Load database credentials and embedding-service credentials from environment variables or a secret manager rather than hardcoding them.
Exclude real .env files from version control and keep only placeholder values in .env.example.
Redact database connection strings, passwords, and API keys from application logs and exception responses.
Give the runtime database identity only the catalog read permissions it needs, and use a separate provisioning identity for seeding and index creation.
Restrict database network access to application hosts through private networking or narrowly scoped firewall rules.
Store each product's title, description, embedding, and display metadata together in one document so a vector-search result does not require a second database lookup.
Assign each catalog product a stable _id and seed it with update_one using upsert=true rather than unconditional insert_one calls.
Store monetary prices as integer minor units or Decimal128 rather than binary floating-point values.
Record the embedding model identifier and a hash or version of the embedded source text alongside each product embedding.
Regenerate a product's embedding whenever its embedded title or description changes.
Keep embeddings from different models in separate vector fields or collections rather than searching them as one shared vector space.
Use the same text-embedding-ada-002 model for catalog embeddings and query embeddings.
Configure the vector index with dimensions=1536 for text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings.
Store embeddings as flat BSON arrays of finite numeric values, not strings, nested arrays, or serialized JSON.
Validate that every stored and query embedding has exactly 1536 elements before submitting it to Azure DocumentDB.
Embed a deterministic combination of the product title and description rather than embedding only the title.
Respect text-embedding-ada-002's input-token limit by rejecting or deterministically truncating oversized embedding input.
Batch catalog embedding requests during seeding instead of making one network request per product.
Reuse a stored embedding during repeated seeding when both the source-text hash and embedding model identifier are unchanged.
Create the native IVF index with a key such as {"embedding":"cosmosSearch"} and cosmosSearchOptions containing kind="vector-ivf", dimensions=1536, similarity="COS", and an explicit numLists.
Use numLists=1 for the 20-product sample rather than a large IVF partition count intended for a substantial catalog.
Populate the representative catalog before creating the IVF index so its partitioning is based on actual vectors.
Give the vector index a stable name and inspect list_indexes before attempting to create it again.
Check an existing vector index's dimensions, similarity, kind, and numLists against the requested configuration instead of treating its name alone as proof of compatibility.
Create catalog data and vector indexes in an explicit seed or migration command rather than during Flask module import or every request.
Execute native vector search with an aggregation $search stage containing cosmosSearch.vector, cosmosSearch.path="embedding", and cosmosSearch.k=10.
Place the vector $search stage first in the aggregation pipeline.
Project the native vector score with {"$meta":"searchScore"} instead of recomputing similarity in Flask.
Preserve the vector-search result order when returning products rather than re-sorting results by a catalog field.
Exclude the embedding field from the /search response with an explicit aggregation projection.
Push category, availability, or tenant restrictions into the vector-search filter rather than filtering only after the top 10 neighbors have been selected.
Create ordinary indexes for catalog fields used in equality filters or product lookups instead of assuming the vector index accelerates those operations.
Tune IVF numLists and query nProbes against measured recall and latency as the catalog grows.
Compare approximate IVF results against an exact cosine-similarity baseline on a representative query set.
Validate that POST /search receives a JSON object with a nonempty string query before calling the embedding service.
Construct the aggregation pipeline from server-controlled fields rather than accepting a client-supplied MongoDB query or pipeline.
Apply a finite maxTimeMS to the vector aggregation so database execution cannot consume the entire request budget indefinitely.
Serialize BSON values such as ObjectId into a documented JSON-safe representation before returning Flask responses.
Retry transient database connectivity failures with bounded exponential backoff and jitter.
Retry embedding-service rate limits and transient server failures with bounded backoff that honors Retry-After.
Retry catalog writes only through an idempotent operation keyed by the stable product identifier.
Do not retry authentication failures, malformed vectors, or invalid index definitions as though they were transient failures.
Provision a cluster tier and service version that support native vector-ivf indexes before deploying the search application.
Size cluster memory for the vector index and expected concurrent searches rather than sizing only for the BSON catalog storage.
Expose a readiness check that verifies database connectivity and the required vector index without reseeding the catalog.
Measure embedding-service latency separately from database vector-search latency.
Run an integration test against Azure DocumentDB that creates the IVF index and executes the actual $search pipeline instead of relying only on MongoDB mocks.
Pin compatible PyMongo and embedding-SDK versions in the dependency configuration.
Deploy Flask behind a production WSGI server with debug mode disabled rather than exposing the Flask development server.
Rate-limit the public search endpoint to bound embedding-service cost and database load.
Enable a defined backup and restore policy before treating the catalog as production data.
